summary: Iloperidone (FANAPT) is an atypical antipsychotic for schizophrenia and acute manic or mixed episodes of bipolar I disorder in adults, acting through combined D2 and 5-HT2A antagonism. It must be slowly titrated from 1 mg twice daily to avoid orthostatic hypotension. Key concerns are QT prolongation, metabolic changes, orthostasis/syncope, and the antipsychotic class boxed warning of increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis (not an approved use). Reduce dose by half in CYP2D6 poor metabolizers or with strong CYP2D6/CYP3A4 inhibitors.
indications: Acute treatment of manic or mixed episodes associated with bipolar I disorder in adults

dosage.d: Start 1 mg twice daily; titrate over ~7 days to target 6-12 mg twice daily
dosage.n: Max 24 mg/day; slow titration limits orthostatic hypotension

dosage.d: Start 1 mg twice daily; titrate over ~5 days to 12 mg twice daily

dosage.c: CYP2D6 poor metabolizers / strong CYP2D6 or CYP3A4 inhibitor
dosage.n: Return to prior dose when inhibitor withdrawn
Not recommended in severe hepatic impairment

dosage.d: Restart with initial titration if off therapy >3 days

admin: Administer orally twice daily, with or without food
Always begin at 1 mg twice daily and titrate gradually to minimize orthostatic hypotension
Use the titration pack appropriate to the indication (schizophrenia vs bipolar)
Obtain baseline ECG; correct hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia before and during therapy
If therapy is interrupted for more than a few days, re-titrate from the starting dose
moa: Iloperidone's therapeutic mechanism is not fully established but is thought to be mediated by combined antagonism of dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT2A receptors. It has high affinity for 5-HT2A, D2, D3 and noradrenergic alpha-1 receptors; the alpha-1 blockade underlies its prominent orthostatic hypotension. It forms an active metabolite (P88) with a similar receptor profile.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to iloperidone or any formulation component (anaphylaxis, angioedema reported)
relative: Congenital long QT syndrome or history of cardiac arrhythmias
Elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis (increased mortality - not approved)
History of seizures or conditions lowering seizure threshold
monitor: ECG/QTc and serum potassium and magnesium
CBC in patients with pre-existing low WBC

preg: Limited human data; not adequate to establish risk of major birth defects. Neonates exposed in the third trimester are at risk for extrapyramidal and/or withdrawal symptoms (agitation, hypertonia, hypotonia, tremor, somnolence, respiratory distress, feeding disorder) after delivery. Use only if the potential benefit justifies the risk; a pregnancy exposure registry for atypical antipsychotics exists.
lact: There are no data on the presence of iloperidone in human milk or its effects on the breastfed infant. Advise women not to breastfeed during treatment.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is provided for renal impairment; iloperidone has not been adequately studied in severe renal impairment - use with caution.
hepatic: No adjustment needed for mild impairment. Iloperidone is NOT recommended in patients with severe hepatic impairment because exposure and toxicity may increase.

major: Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors (fluoxetine, paroxetine) - increase iloperidone/P88; reduce iloperidone dose by half
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole) - increase iloperidone exposure; reduce dose by half
Other QT-prolonging drugs (class IA/III antiarrhythmics, some antipsychotics, certain antibiotics) - avoid; additive QT prolongation/arrhythmia risk
minor: Drugs causing electrolyte loss (diuretics) - increase QT risk via hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; high-fat meals delay but do not significantly reduce absorption.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol; it adds to sedation and hypotension.
interactions.diagnostics: Prolongs the QTc interval; may raise prolactin, glucose, lipids and liver enzymes.

serious: QT-interval prolongation with risk of arrhythmia
emergency: Torsades de pointes / sudden cardiac arrest
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (hyperthermia, rigidity, autonomic instability)

monitoring: Serum potassium and magnesium in at-risk patients
Blood pressure and heart rate, especially orthostatic, during titration
Fasting glucose, lipid panel and weight/BMI
CBC in patients with pre-existing low WBC or history of leukopenia
counsel: This medicine is started low and increased slowly - do not skip the titration steps
You may feel dizzy or faint, especially when standing up quickly or early in treatment; rise slowly
Avoid alcohol and tell your doctor about all other medicines, especially heart-rhythm drugs
Report fainting, palpitations, high fever with muscle stiffness, uncontrolled movements, or a painful prolonged erection
Watch for weight gain and increased thirst/urination; blood sugar, cholesterol and weight will be checked
pk: Gradual over titration; steady state in 3-4 days
~18 h (iloperidone) in extensive metabolizers; ~33 h in poor metabolizers
Store at 25 C (excursions 15-30 C); protect from light and moisture
pearls: Boxed warning: increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis - not approved for that use
Slow mandatory titration from 1 mg BID is the price of its low EPS/akathisia profile (alpha-1 blockade causes orthostasis)
Notable QT prolongation - avoid combining with other QT-prolonging drugs and correct electrolytes
Halve the dose in CYP2D6 poor metabolizers and with strong CYP2D6/CYP3A4 inhibitors
Not recommended in severe hepatic impairment
missed: If a dose is missed, take it when remembered unless it is close to the next dose - then skip it; do not double up. If therapy is interrupted for more than a few days, contact the prescriber, as re-titration from the starting dose is required.
overdose: No specific antidote. Expect exaggerated pharmacologic effects (drowsiness, sedation, tachycardia, hypotension) and possible QT prolongation/arrhythmia, seizures and dystonia. Maintain airway and oxygenation, consider gastric lavage/activated charcoal, and start continuous ECG monitoring. Avoid disopyramide, procainamide and quinidine (additive QT effects); treat hypotension/circulatory collapse with fluids and pressors (not bretylium).
